reason: The children are an objection argued at length about action and time and the Vaibhasika reply, a real dispute.
Each child is a one-sentence gloss of a verse line on how abandoned things remain possessed, for seeing- and meditation-abandonables.
The children analyse in detail which minds take each realm's abandonables as object, the first with its own three-part breakdown.
The children explain the sequence in which the afflictions arise and their causes, including a note on the Sautrantika objection.
The children mainly identify which afflictions make up each of the three asravas, with short supporting reasons.
The children are verse glosses giving the etymologies of anusaya and of asrava and related terms.
The children explain the nine fetters and the lower and higher fetters with reasons, answered doubts and the Cittamatra view.
The children discuss the envelopments and stains, their causes and distinctions, including the Vaibhasika view, disputed points and a scriptural story.
The children list which feelings the root afflictions occur with in the desire realm and the higher realms (the second is a one-line pointer).
The children raise and answer why paired obscurations count as one and argue why there are exactly five, citing antidotes, nutriments and functions.
The children identify which anusayas are abandoned by each of the three modes of abandonment.
The children are one-line definitions of the four kinds of antidote, splitting a single sentence.
The children are list items naming the four kinds of distance, splitting one sentence.
The children explain which paths and levels yield which full knowledges, with Vaibhasika and Bhadanta Ghosaka positions argued.
The first child raises a doubt about why there are not more full knowledges and answers it with three reasons; the second is a short gloss.
The children explain the four truths' nature, argue their order with an analogy, and discuss the three kinds of suffering with sutra citations.
The children explain the progression of hearing, reflection and meditation and contrast the Vaibhasika and the Master's views on the three wisdoms.
The children discuss discontent and great desire, contrasting the Abhidharmikas' and the Master's definitions, and their antidotes.
The second child explains the four noble lineages at length, with sutra citations and their purpose against craving.
The children teach the meditation on the unattractive, covering its practice stages, antidotes and special qualities.
The children explain mindfulness of breathing in detail: its levels, its six aspects, the nature of breath and who can perceive it.
The children explain the method, nature, order and number of the applications of mindfulness, with differing views and sutra citations.
The children explain how heat, peak, patience and supreme dharma arise and their shared features, each with its own reasoning.
The children discuss the levels, bases, loss, benefits and lineage of the aids to penetration, with Ghosaka's view and nested sub-points.
The children are one-line definitions of the three kinds of realization, splitting a single sentence.
The children are short verse glosses that sort the sixteen moments into the two paths and give the meaning of the name 'path of seeing'.
The children define the two kinds of person (faith-follower and dharma-follower) and identify who counts as entering the first fruit.
The children are one-line definitions of entering the once-returner and the non-returner fruits.
The children briefly identify the fruit-abider at the sixteenth moment and give the names used for dull and sharp faculties.
The children raise and answer why the fruit-abider is not an enterer, and explain the ninefold grading of paths and afflictions with reasons.
The first child discusses the 'seven times' rebirth with Vaibhasika and other views and resolves an objection from a sutra.
The second child explains the once-returner with one interval and the doubt it is meant to remove; the first is a one-line definition.
The children explain the five kinds of non-returner and those who go higher in detail, with differing views on order and nirvana.
The children discuss subdivisions of non-returners, the Good Person's courses, change of life and mixed meditation, with objections and sutra citations.
